content:
Dear Corvale Mobility Hiring Team,

I’m applying for the Cloud Infrastructure / DevOps Contractor – Fleet Connectivity role. I’m a QA automation engineer with seven years of experience, including the last two focused primarily on CI/CD pipelines, test environments and build tooling. I’m now looking to move into DevOps and platform engineering full time, and the opportunity to help shape infrastructure for Corvale’s new train fleet is a compelling next step.

At Odrava Health, I own GitLab CI pipelines used by three product teams, covering builds, tests and artifact publishing. By profiling the pipelines, parallelising jobs, adding dependency caching and separating end-to-end tests into their own stage, I reduced average pipeline time from 38 to 14 minutes and monthly runner costs by about 30%. I also built short-lived merge-request environments using Docker Compose and Helm on a shared Kubernetes cluster, and wrote internal CI documentation now used in onboarding. This work has taught me to make infrastructure workflows practical for the teams that depend on them and to communicate changes clearly.

I’ve also built a personal three-node k3s cluster, deploying applications through Argo CD and setting up Prometheus, Grafana, Loki, Traefik and cert-manager. I used Terraform to provision infrastructure for a small Hetzner VPS, and have explored AWS through basic EC2 and S3 learning. My Kubernetes work at Odrava is at namespace level on a shared cluster, where I create Helm deployments for test environments. I would bring this hands-on experience, along with a careful, analytical approach, to Corvale’s work on reliable and observable fleet connectivity.

Corvale’s engineering-led approach and emphasis on teams owning their systems end to end appeal to me. I’d welcome the opportunity to discuss how my experience improving delivery infrastructure and building test environments could contribute to the Fleet Connectivity team.

Thank you for your time and consideration.

Marta Kowal-Brandt

critique.content_quality_feedback: The cover letter is clear, professional, truthful, and appropriately tailored to the Fleet Connectivity role. It presents strong evidence of CI/CD improvement, ephemeral environments, Kubernetes-related work, observability, and measurable results. The quantified pipeline improvement and cost reduction are especially persuasive. The progression from QA automation toward DevOps/platform engineering is explained credibly. However, the letter spends substantial space on tools and personal infrastructure without clearly distinguishing the candidate’s production scope from personal or shared-cluster experience. It also does not directly address the role’s emphasis on technical leadership, systems design, secure connectivity, or stakeholder alignment. The final paragraph references Corvale’s engineering-led culture appropriately, but the connection to the specific Fleet Connectivity responsibilities could be more concrete.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The document is ATS- and AI-readable: it uses standard paragraphs, contains the exact job title, and includes relevant supported keywords such as GitLab CI, Docker, Helm, Kubernetes, Argo CD, Prometheus, Grafana, Loki, Terraform, AWS, EC2, and S3. The plain-text structure and absence of tables, graphics, unusual symbols, or excessive formatting are parsing-friendly. AI screening probability is moderate rather than high because several prominent requirements are either absent or only indirectly addressed: Terragrunt, systems architecture/system design, networking, mutual TLS, practical security, stakeholder leadership, and Linux. The letter correctly avoids claiming unsupported production AWS, Terraform, Kubernetes-cluster administration, or security experience. Terraform is mentioned, but its personal-project scope should remain explicit so that the document does not imply strong professional Terraform experience.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The strongest alignment is with hands-on infrastructure-adjacent engineering, CI/CD, analytical problem-solving, observability, clear technical communication, and support for teams deploying and testing services. The candidate has credible evidence of owning GitLab CI pipelines, creating Kubernetes-based ephemeral environments, improving reliability and performance, documenting workflows, and operating a personal k3s/GitOps environment. This supports parts of the platform reliability and developer enablement scope. The main gaps are strong Terraform and Terragrunt, cloud environment design and operation at the required level, systems architecture/system design, networking including mTLS and SSL/TLS, practical security awareness, IoT or remote-device integration, and backend/full-stack experience. The candidate material does not show production on-call or production cloud ownership, so the letter appropriately does not claim them. Technical leadership and stakeholder alignment are only partially evidenced through pipeline ownership, onboarding documentation, and environments used by QA and product teams.
critique.improvement_instructions:
CRITICAL ISSUES:
1. In the paragraph beginning “At Odrava Health,” make the stakeholder and technical-leadership evidence explicit without overstating authority. After the sentence about the internal CI documentation, add a truthful sentence such as: “I also documented the CI workflow for onboarding and built merge-request environments that enabled QA and product teams to review features and run end-to-end tests before merge.” This directly supports the requirement to lead technical topics and bring stakeholders along, using evidence already present in the candidate material.
2. In the paragraph beginning “I’ve also built a personal three-node k3s cluster,” clarify the scope of the Terraform and Kubernetes experience to prevent an overly senior interpretation. Replace “I used Terraform to provision infrastructure for a small Hetzner VPS” with “In a personal project, I used Terraform to provision infrastructure for a small Hetzner VPS.” Retain the existing sentence explaining that the Odrava Kubernetes work is at namespace level on a shared cluster. This preserves truthfulness while presenting the experience precisely.
3. In the same infrastructure paragraph, connect the observability experience more directly to the job’s supported platform language. Replace “I would bring this hands-on experience, along with a careful, analytical approach, to Corvale’s work on reliable and observable fleet connectivity” with “I would bring this hands-on experience, careful analytical approach, and focus on observable, reliable delivery workflows to Corvale’s Fleet Connectivity team.” This avoids implying prior fleet-connectivity experience while making the transferable alignment clearer.

MINOR ENHANCEMENT:
4. In the opening paragraph, replace “test environments and build tooling” with “CI/CD pipelines, Kubernetes-based test environments, build tooling and internal infrastructure automation.” This uses supported terminology from the associated CV and makes the DevOps/platform relevance clearer at the start of the letter.

I’m now looking to move into DevOps and platform engineering full time, and the opportunity to help shape infrastructure for Corvale’s new train fleet is a compelling next step.

I also documented the CI workflow for onboarding and built merge-request environments that enabled QA and product teams to review features and run end-to-end tests before merge. This work has taught me to make infrastructure workflows practical for the teams that depend on them and to communicate changes clearly.

Corvale’s engineering-led approach and emphasis on teams owning their systems end to end appeal to me. I’d welcome the opportunity to discuss how my experience improving delivery infrastructure and building test environments could contribute to the Fleet Connectivity team.

Thank you for your time and consideration.

Marta Kowal-Brandt

critique.content_quality_feedback: The cover letter is professional, readable, and appropriately tailored to the Fleet Connectivity role. It uses strong quantified achievements, including reducing pipeline time from 38 to 14 minutes and runner costs by about 30%, and it accurately explains the candidate's transition from QA automation into DevOps/platform engineering. The main content weakness is repetition: the second paragraph states the CI documentation and merge-request environment achievements twice. The letter also spends some space on the career transition rather than concentrating on the strongest evidence of infrastructure engineering, observability, Terraform, Kubernetes, and stakeholder collaboration.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The letter is ATS-readable: it uses standard paragraphs, no problematic layout elements, and includes relevant supported keywords such as CI/CD, GitLab CI, Kubernetes, Docker Compose, Helm, Terraform, AWS, EC2, S3, Argo CD, Prometheus, Grafana, Loki, and TLS. AI screening probability is moderate rather than high because several central requirements—Terragrunt, mTLS, networking, systems architecture, and security—are not demonstrated in the candidate material and therefore cannot be added. The letter could also use the exact supported phrase "infrastructure engineering" and make the existing stakeholder-facing work more explicit without overstating scope.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The candidate is a credible developing DevOps/platform candidate with strong evidence of CI/CD ownership, ephemeral environments, Kubernetes-based delivery, infrastructure automation, observability, analytical improvement, and technical documentation. The letter aligns well with Corvale's engineering-led and ownership-oriented culture through its emphasis on practical workflows and teams depending on infrastructure. However, the candidate's material shows gaps against several core requirements: strong Terraform and Terragrunt, systems architecture/system design, networking including mTLS, practical security depth, and train/IoT/remote-device integration. The candidate has Terraform experience in a personal Hetzner project but no Terragrunt; TLS through cert-manager but no demonstrated mTLS; and Java test automation rather than backend or full-stack JVM experience. These are role-fit gaps, not defects that can be solved by rewriting the letter.
critique.improvement_instructions:
CRITICAL: In the second paragraph, remove the repeated claims about documentation and merge-request environments. After the sentence ending "monthly runner costs fell by about 30%," retain one concise version of the environment achievement and one concise version of the documentation achievement. For example: "I also built short-lived merge-request environments using Docker Compose and Helm on a shared Kubernetes cluster, enabling QA and product teams to review features and run end-to-end tests before merge. I authored the internal CI workflow guide, which is now used for onboarding." Delete the later sentences beginning "I also documented the CI workflow..." and "I also documented the CI workflow for onboarding..." so each achievement appears only once.

MINOR: In the opening paragraph, replace "focused primarily on CI/CD pipelines, Kubernetes-based test environments, build tooling and internal infrastructure automation" with "focused primarily on CI/CD pipelines, Kubernetes-based test environments, build tooling and infrastructure engineering". This uses the job's supported terminology without claiming cloud infrastructure ownership beyond the evidence provided.

MINOR: In the third paragraph, make the existing Linux experience visible by changing "I’ve also built a personal three-node k3s cluster" to "I’ve also built and operated a personal three-node k3s cluster on Linux-based Raspberry Pi nodes." This is supported by the candidate information and improves alignment with the Linux requirement.

MINOR: In the paragraph describing Corvale fit, make stakeholder communication more concrete by changing "careful analytical approach" to "analytical approach, clear technical documentation and experience enabling QA and product stakeholders to review changes safely". This is directly supported by the merge-request environments and internal CI workflow guide and better reflects the requirement to bring stakeholders along.

MINOR: Keep the AWS wording qualified. Do not change "basic EC2 and S3 learning" into production AWS experience, cloud architecture ownership, or AWS operations, because the candidate information states that AWS experience is limited to free-tier learning.
